lead: The definitive itinerary to discover the best of the city on the Turia: historic centre, Albufera, beaches and the City of Arts and Sciences.

Three days are enough to discover the essence of Valencia: its rich medieval heritage, the landscapes of the Albufera natural park, the urban beaches of the Mediterranean and the spectacular architectural complex of the City of Arts and Sciences.
This itinerary, designed from the official guides of Visit València and Turisme Comunitat Valenciana, organises each day so you make the most of your time without giving up anything essential.

items.title: Heritage, markets and El Carmen district
items.body: Valencia’s old town packs centuries of history into a maze of streets and squares. From the Cathedral and the Holy Chalice to La Lonja de la Seda, a World Heritage Site, by way of the Modernista bustle of the Central Market and the bohemian atmosphere of El Carmen.
facts: Climb the 207 steps for the best views of the historic centre
Plaza de la Virgen and Plaza de la Reina
The symbolic heart of the city, setting for the Fallas flower offering
The Valencian Sistine Chapel: almost 2,000 m² of Baroque frescoes on its vaults
A masterpiece of civil Gothic, a World Heritage Site since 1996
More than 250 stalls beneath an early 20th-century Modernista dome
Street art, the IVAM, the Centre del Carme and the Serranos Towers at the end of the walk
notes: Start early at the Cathedral before the tour groups arrive. The Central Market closes at 15:00: use it for a mid-morning esmorzaret.

items.title: Nature, paella and cutting-edge Valencia
items.body: A morning in L’Albufera Natural Park to discover the origin of Valencian paella aboard a traditional boat, and an afternoon between the Bioparc and La Marina, with the best Mediterranean sunsets from Malvarrosa beach.
facts: 10 km from the centre: rice fields, lake, wildlife and a boat trip on the Albufera
A fishing hamlet where you can try authentic Valencian paella in its place of origin
Immersion in the African savanna with more than 4,000 animals of 160 species
A seafaring district with popular Modernisme, unique tiles and emerging gastronomy
More than 2 km of golden sand with seafront restaurants
Marina de València and Veles e Vents
David Chipperfield’s building and the best sunset with the Mediterranean as a backdrop
notes: For the Albufera take bus 24 or 25 from the centre (included in the València Tourist Card). Book a table in El Palmar in advance at weekends.

items.title: The future on the banks of the river
items.body: The old bed of the River Turia, transformed into 9 kilometres of car-free urban park, links the heart of the city with Valencia’s most iconic skyline: the City of Arts and Sciences, designed by Santiago Calatrava, with the Oceanogràfic, the Museu de les Ciències and the Hemisfèric.
facts: 9 km of linear park: ideal on foot or by bike, with the Bioparc at one end and the CAC at the other
Museu de les Ciències Príncipe Felipe
Interactive science in a building that looks like the skeleton of a prehistoric animal
Europe’s largest aquarium: more than 500 species from the Mediterranean and other seas
Spain’s largest concave 3D cinema screen, with 900 m² of projection
Umbracle and Palau de les Arts
The sculpture garden and the great opera house that closes the complex
Turia Gardens · City of Arts and Sciences
notes: Buy CAC tickets online to avoid queues. If you cycle from the centre, the ride along the Turia Gardens to the CAC takes about 35 minutes without effort.

blocks.title: Practical tips
items: The València Tourist Card includes unlimited transport and discounts at monuments
Buses 24 and 25 go to the Albufera: activate them with the Tourist Card
The Central Market closes at 15:00 and does not open on Sundays
San Nicolás and La Lonja require online booking in advance
The Turia Gardens are the green axis that links the three days of the itinerary
The València Tourist Card comes in 24, 48 and 72-hour versions
